item.title: Identity Politics (Ep. 168): They Forgot The Alamo
item.description: The Republican Party has turned Texas into the Lone Saar State and is now attacking those who dare to notice the problem of mass immigration by Indians. Yet if the GOP can't defend someone like Bo French, they can hardly defend the existence of Texas itself. Identity isn't an "idea," but something inherent, and those who say otherwise are simply trying to destroy you. Plus, Connor Tomlinson joins to discuss the rising nationalist resistance in Great Britain, the government's crackdown on street protests, and the potential breakup of the UK itself.

item.title: Identity Politics (Ep. 167): Financial Accelerationism
item.description: Even on the brink of political ruin, Republicans are quibbling about limited government, fiscal conservatism, and "true conservative principles." Well, unless someone has General Pinochet on ice, none of these are serious proposals. In fact, given that fiscal ruin is basically certain given universal suffrage, we might as well lean into it. It's not financial nihilism - it's about getting serious about the nature of the system we live under and preparing for what comes next.

item.title: Identity Politics (Ep. 166): England Lives
item.description: English patriots are rising in Portsmouth and Dover, taking direct action to stop the occupation government's efforts to settle foreign migrants in their communities. Naturally, the same government that claims it can't stop immigration is championing repression against its own people, and far too many right-wingers are going along with it. Nationalist leaders need to stop counter-signaling and start defending their own. Plus, Alexandre Cormier-Denis of Nomos TV joins to speak about his speech at the Dominion Society and the nationalist struggle in Quebec.

item.title: Identity Politics (Ep. 165): Germany Awakes
item.description: The nationalist AfD has won a major victory in regional elections in Germany, and the government is panicking. But the party faces difficult choices when it comes to forming a government. If the nationalist movement in America develops correctly, the questions they face may soon be our own. What conservatives, if any, can be won over? Are there any elements of the Left who can serve as allies? And perhaps most importantly, is it best to refuse responsibility in government until you can rule independently? Plus, Daniel Tyrie of the Dominion Society returns to give us the inside story on the successful conference that has shocked the system in the Great White North.

item.title: Identity Politics (Ep. 164): State of the Right
item.description: A week from today will be the one year anniversary of the assassination of Charlie Kirk. In the year since, the American Right seems to have totally fractured. The Trump Administration has scored some successes against antifa, but its coalition is splintering. Part of this is due to the Administration's missteps. However, part of it is due to our own vanguard, which is desperate to opt out of conflict, make a separate peace, and take refuge in "safe edgy" conspiracy theories that keep you out of trouble.
